decision: rejected any candidate with raddr in the local-link filter

decision: measured browser deflate on 8 MB blocks of realistic files
why: most people are upload-bound, so fewer bytes is the one lever that helps them
result: logs 5%, tar 16%, json 22%, csv 23%, bmp 58%, zip/random ~100%; 67-300 MB/s compress; 64 KB probe predicts within ~3 points

decision: chose per-block deflate-raw, gated by a 64 KB probe and by compressor speed vs link speed
why: skips media that won't shrink, and never slows a link faster than the compressor

decision: built compressed blocks: receiver opts in on start, sender sends a z header then deflated bytes
why: keeps old pages working and lets the receiver bound every size before inflating

decision: added a 1 MB/s coturn relay to test against a home-upload-sized link
why: the local link is too fast to show what compression does for internet transfers

decision: wrote attack tests for compressed blocks: bomb, corrupt, short, oversized, truncated
why: a sender who knows the secret is untrusted, and inflating is new attack surface

decision: benchmarked compression off vs on through the 1 MB/s relay, 3 alternating runs per file
why: to measure the gain on an upload-sized link
result: median: logs 37x, json 4.8x, csv 4.4x, tar 3x, bmp 1.4x, zip and random unchanged; 42/42 intact

decision: reran random data 5 alternating times after an apparent 15% slowdown
why: 3 runs suggested a regression the code couldn't explain
result: no difference: medians 13.7s off vs 11.6s on, ranges overlap

decision: receiver progress now counts arriving bytes, scaling compressed ones
why: progress froze 6-9 s per compressed block on a slow link

decision: link.mjs refuses to run when a local server serves an older page than the disk

decision: checked compression on the fast local link with a 109 MB photo, 2 alternating pairs

decision: measured where connect time goes on the live site

decision: send each description 250 ms after the last candidate, once the needed types are in
